title: POC scoping - Data handling & retention (Acme Health)
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling requirements for a 4-week POC: PII redaction, log retention, prompt storage, encryption/KMS, and success criteria including latency/throughput benchmarks and timeline. Agreed to start integration next week and run two benchmark workloads (extraction + summarization) with 10k examples each. Security docs and retention matrix to be shared.
action_items: Sophie Martinez - Share security datasheet and SOC2 summary - 2025-07-24
Daniel Cho - Provide benchmark harness and sample load script (k6 + python) - 2025-07-25
Priya Patel - Provide redaction rules and sample dataset (10k) - 2025-07-24
Carlos Ruiz - Send Acme retention policy and legal requirements for PHI - 2025-07-23
Sophie Martinez - Schedule kickoff integration call & invite infra (Jared) - 2025-07-23
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and data handling whitepaper (link)
Customer to upload sample dataset to secure S3 bucket; Redwood will pull via presigned URL or set up VPC peering
Schedule 60-min integration kick-off to configure logging/retention and test client-side redaction flow
Run two benchmark suites (extraction, summarization) over next 2 weeks and share results
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Head of ML, Acme Health), Carlos Ruiz (Security/Compliance), Dr. Emily Hart (Product), Jared Lin (Platform), Nina Gomez (Legal)

--- Optional autogenerated summary ---
Sophie (00:00): hey everyone thanks for joining, we want to make sure we cover your data handling constraints for the POC and confirm success criteria and timelines
Priya (00:18): thanks, yes our top concerns are PHI/PII, where prompts might leak sensitive fields, and retention of logs we need to be very strict here
Daniel (00:35): quick intro from our side, i'll be the SE on the bench side, we'll provide the harness and help configure retention settings; you'll mostly choose whether to run hosted or dedicated for the POC depending on network/region needs
Carlos (00:53): to be explicit, any storage of PHI needs to be encrypted at rest with CMKs and we need audit logs for any access, plus SSO and RBAC for anyone who can see the raw prompts
Sophie (01:12): understood, we have KMS integration and HSM options and support SAML/SSO + RBAC. we'll share SOC 2 and our security pack after the call

[01:45] Daniel: ok let's walk through data flows for the POC, there are a few options - 1) client-side redaction before sending, 2) server-side redaction in transit, or 3) tokenization / synthetic replace on the client and then post-process. each has tradeoffs for eval accuracy.
Priya (02:12): client-side redaction is preferred because legal wants PHI not to leave our environment unredacted, but we need to understand how that affects model performance for extraction tasks
Daniel (02:38): yeah often with client-side redaction you replace e.g., dob -> [DOB_REDACTED], name-> [NAME], which keeps the structure but preserves task signal in many cases. we can run ablation tests. note transcription sometimes shows kv-cache as k-v cash which is fine - pricing, not relevant here :)

[04:05] Carlos: what about logging on the Redwood side? we need logs for troubleshooting but cannot retain raw prompts beyond an agreed retention window, and they must be encrypted and access controlled.
Sophie (04:28): our platform supports configurable logging tiers. for POC we can set logs to 'errors-only' and scrub full prompt text; we also support retention policies down to 30 days or custom retention on Dedicated/VPC installs. for hosted, default retention is 90 days but we can set 30 days for trial or provide ephemeral logs if necessary.
Carlos (04:57): ephemeral logs sound good. also need to confirm whether debug logs ever contain full prompt in plaintext when tracing.
Daniel (05:12): debug traces can contain prompt payloads; for the POC we will disable debug-level traces and enable structured redaction. we also have a redaction pipeline that runs regex and fuzzy detectors. we'll share the rule set but you should provide the PHI patterns you want matched.

[06:10] Dr. Emily Hart: from product side, success criteria - we need end-to-end accuracy on extraction >= 92% on the sample set and latency p95 < 450ms on average for 128-token responses. throughput target for our POC is 200 qps sustained for a 1-hour soak. that would be representative of pilot workload.
Sophie (06:36): noted. we've seen similar benchmarks on our bench for models like redwood-v2-small, but depending on quantization and batching p95 can vary. Daniel will propose config (batch size, kv cache settings, quantization) to meet latency.

[07:10] Priya: about prompt storage — we use prompt templates containing PHI fields replaced at runtime. is there a way to avoid storing filled prompts on Redwood?
Daniel (07:28): yes, two ways: 1) store only templates server-side and send only filled-in prompts transiently (we don't persist them), or 2) if you must persist filled prompts for audit, store them encrypted with customer-managed keys and set retention policies. VPC/private installs give you full control. Hosted can support CMK wrapping but we'll need KMS integration and an agreement for key handling.
Priya (07:58): ideal is not to persist filled prompts. we may keep templates and store redacted transcripts only.

[09:05] Sophie: for benchmarks, we propose two workloads: (A) structured extraction, 10k examples, target metric accuracy; (B) long-form summarization, 10k examples, target latency/p95. run each workload with a 1-hour ramp + 3-hour steady run and capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates. does that sound reasonable?
Priya (09:32): yes that's fine, and include a stability 24-hour run if initial tests look good.

[10:00] Carlos: for compliance please confirm: 1) audit logs for all admin access to logs and keys, 2) no staff access to prompt contents without explicit access request logged, 3) support for paper/eDiscovery if needed.
Daniel (10:20): we produce audit logs for admin operations and key unwrap events; staff access is gated by RBAC and logged. note that in the hosted mode we manage the control plane; in Dedicated or Private your security team gets more control (and more visibility into logs locally).

[12:15] Nina (Legal): any NDA or DPA changes needed for PHI? we will send a redlined DPA after the call.
Sophie (12:30): we'll review and coordinate with legal — appreciate the redline.

[13:05] Priya: about encryption — we require CMEK for any persisted prompts or logs with PHI. is that supported?
Sophie (13:20): yes, we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via KMS providers and HSM in Private deployments. for hosted we can integrate with your cloud KMS and configure key rotation policies.

[14:00] Daniel: a note on redaction fidelity: regex only can miss edge cases; we recommend combining regex with ML-based detectors (fuzzy match) and a small review step. for the POC we can run both and compare false-negative rates.

[16:10] Priya: timeline? we'd like a 4-week POC starting next Monday. week1: integration + data upload + redaction rules; week2: run extraction benchmarks; week3: run summarization benchmarks + stability; week4: evaluation and decision.
Sophie (16:35): that timeline works for us. we'll allocate an AE+SE and provide a priority contact. we'll also provide a sample benchmarking harness and scripts.

[18:00] Jared (Platform): network question — we need VPC peering or private link for hosted peering. what are options?
Daniel (18:15): supported options: presigned S3 URLs for data pulls, VPC peering, PrivateLink/Private Service Connect depending on cloud. Dedicated and Private give more flexibility. we'll put the networking options in the runbook.

[20:05] Carlos: any concerns about model caching or shared KV cache leaking cross-tenant context?
Daniel (20:25): our runtime isolates KV caches per request/tenant. in older transcripts/notes sometimes 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K V cash' but rest assured caches are tenant-isolated. we also evict caches on session end if configured.

[22:00] Discussion about benchmarks and measurement details (error budgets, SLOs)
Daniel (22:10): we'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rate, and quality metrics (F1/accuracy) from your labeled sample set. for cost estimates we'll run both quantized and fp16 runs.

[30:00] Priya: what about retention defaults on hosted? you mentioned 90d default. can you make PII logs 30 days?
Sophie (30:18): yes for the POC we can set retention to 30 days and disable full-text logs, keeping only anonymized traces. for longer-term deployments we'll discuss policies.

[36:00] Quick recap and agreed next steps
Sophie (36:12): recap: Redwood to share security pack + benchmark harness; customer to share sample data and redaction rules; kickoff integration next Wednesday. success criteria: accuracy >= 92% extraction, p95 latency < 450ms, throughput 200 qps sustained for 1-hour soak; logs retention 30 days, CMEK required for persisted data.
Priya (36:48): yes and we'll send the DPA redline and retention matrix.

[38:20] Closing
Sophie (38:22): thanks all, we'll follow up with links and invite.
Priya (38:30): thanks everyone.
